examDifficulty.heading: Is the OmniStudio Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam tests how you build OmniStudio solutions and choose the right tool for each task. Know how data moves between OmniScripts, FlexCards, Data Mappers, and Integration Procedures.
bullets: 60 scored questions and up to 5 unscored questions in 105 minutes.
72% passing score. Check the official exam guide before booking.
Choose the right tool. Know when to use an OmniScript, FlexCard, Data Mapper, or Integration Procedure.
Hands-on practice helps. Build an OmniScript that uses a Data Mapper and calls an Integration Procedure.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build an OmniScript that reads Salesforce data with a Data Mapper, calls an Integration Procedure, and saves a result. Practice until you can explain where each value comes from.

examFormat.heading: OmniStudio Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Many questions describe what a user needs to do or what data a system must read or save.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: For each scenario, identify whether the task is a guided user flow, a compact data display, a data read or write, or server-side work. Then choose the OmniStudio tool that fits.
bestWayToPass: Learn the four main tools: OmniScript guides users, FlexCard displays information, Data Mapper reads or writes data, and Integration Procedure runs server-side logic.
Follow the data: Know how values enter a component, move between steps, and return to the caller.
Move complex work server-side: Use an Integration Procedure for heavier work or calls to several systems.
Practice debugging: Use preview and the debug panel to see what data each element receives.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers building with OmniStudio: OmniScripts, FlexCards, Data Mappers, and Integration Procedures, including how these tools work together and how to add custom components. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 72% pass mark, weighted towards Omniscripts (20%) and Omnistudio Fundamentals (18%).

keyConcepts.h2: OmniStudio Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: The Four Main OmniStudio Tools
blocks.body: **OmniScript** guides a user through steps, collects information, and shows results. It can support tasks such as opening an account or changing a plan. **FlexCard** displays a compact summary of a record and can offer actions, such as opening an OmniScript. A **Data Mapper** (formerly DataRaptor) reads, transforms, or writes data. **Integration Procedure** runs server-side logic, calls other services, and combines results. Many exam questions ask which of these tools best fits a task.

blocks.heading: Data Mapper: Extract, Load, and Transform
blocks.body: A **Data Mapper Extract** reads Salesforce data and returns it in a format such as JSON. **Data Mapper Load** writes input data to Salesforce records. **Data Mapper Transform** changes data from one shape to another without reading or writing Salesforce records. **Turbo Extract** is a faster option for simpler reads from one Salesforce object and related records, but it has fewer configuration options. Use Data Mappers for reusable, declarative data work that admins can update without Apex.

blocks.heading: Integration Procedures and Performance
blocks.body: An **Integration Procedure** runs on the server and can combine several operations in one request. It can call Data Mappers, external services through HTTP actions, and Apex through Remote Actions. A **Chainable** procedure can continue work in another transaction when more processing is needed. **Parallel** elements can run independent calls at the same time. Use an Integration Procedure for server-side work rather than making an OmniScript call out repeatedly.

blocks.heading: OmniScript Structure and Custom Components
blocks.body: An OmniScript contains **steps** and **elements**. Input elements collect data, display elements show it, and action elements read or save data. **Conditional views** show or hide elements based on the user’s answers. The script stores information in JSON, and each element reads from or writes to named keys. When standard elements do not meet a need, a **custom Lightning Web Component** can be placed in the script and exchange data with it. OmniStudio components can also appear on Lightning pages or Experience Cloud sites.

blocks.heading: Debugging, Deployment, and Versions
blocks.body: OmniStudio components use **versions**. Activate the version users need; create a new version to make changes. Preview and the debug panel show the JSON at each step, which helps find missing or unexpected data. Teams can move components between orgs as datapacks and include them in a release process. Record IDs differ across orgs, so hard-coded IDs can cause a component to work in one environment but fail in another.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce OmniStudio Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Start by deciding whether the task happens on screen or on the server, and whether it reads, writes, or reshapes data. Then choose the OmniStudio tool built for that job.

blocks.heading: Design OmniScripts
blocks.body: Use OmniScripts for guided, multi-step user tasks. Show only relevant steps and keep heavy processing out of the script.

blocks.heading: Use Data Mappers
blocks.body: Extract reads data, Load writes data, Transform reshapes data, and Turbo Extract is a faster option for simple reads.

blocks.heading: Use Integration Procedures
blocks.body: Use them for server-side work that combines data or services. Run independent actions in parallel when appropriate.

blocks.heading: Build FlexCards
blocks.body: Use FlexCards to show a compact summary of data and provide actions, often as a starting point for an OmniScript.

blocks.heading: Add a Custom Lightning Web Component
blocks.body: Use a custom component when standard OmniStudio elements cannot meet the need. Pass data through the OmniScript JSON.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio tool guides a user through a series of steps?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An OmniScript guides a user through a step-by-step digital process.
whyWrong: This is the tool designed for guided user experiences.
A Lightning Web Component can extend an interface, but it is not the OmniStudio flow tool described.
Visualforce is a different Salesforce interface technology.

sampleQuestions.question: What can an OmniStudio Data Mapper do?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Mappers can read Salesforce data, transform data, or write data to Salesforce.
whyWrong: This describes the main Data Mapper tasks.
Sending email is not the main purpose of Data Mappers.
Slack messaging is not the purpose of Data Mappers.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio component displays a compact, card-style summary of record data?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A FlexCard displays data in a compact card layout and can offer actions.
whyWrong: This is the component used for compact card-style displays.
An Integration Procedure runs server-side logic.
A Data Mapper reads, transforms, or writes data.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Integration Procedure?
options: An email template that merges record fields into messages sent to customers
A reusable server-side process that can call APIs and Data Mappers
A report that summarizes record data
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Integration Procedure runs server-side steps and can call APIs, Data Mappers, and other actions.
whyWrong: Email templates store message content.
This describes an Integration Procedure.
Reports summarize data; they do not orchestrate server-side actions.

sampleQuestions.question: Which areas commonly use OmniStudio for guided digital processes?
options: Manufacturing companies and no other industries
Schools and universities, but not commercial businesses
Financial Services, Insurance, and other industries
Retail and consumer goods companies exclusively
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio is used across industries, including Financial Services and Insurance.
whyWrong: OmniStudio is not limited to Manufacturing.
OmniStudio is not limited to Education.
This option reflects common OmniStudio use across industries.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Data Mapper Extract do?
options: Transform data without reading or writing records
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Data Mapper Extract reads Salesforce data and returns it in an output format such as JSON.
whyWrong: Writing records is handled by a Data Mapper Load.
Transform changes data structure without reading or writing Salesforce records.
Sending email is not the purpose of an Extract.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniScript element provides a step in the guided flow?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Step element divides an OmniScript into sections the user can complete in order.
whyWrong: FlexCards display compact information; they do not define an OmniScript step.
An Integration Procedure runs server-side logic.
A Data Mapper handles data operations.

sampleQuestions.question: Which data sources can a FlexCard use?
options: Apex, Data Mapper, or Integration Procedure
A parent OmniScript, with no other source allowed
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexCards can use sources such as Apex, a Data Mapper, or an Integration Procedure.
whyWrong: FlexCards can be connected to data sources.
This lists supported kinds of data source.
Email is not the only FlexCard data source.

sampleQuestions.question: What lets an OmniScript show different steps based on data or user input?
options: OmniStudio does not support conditional navigation.
Only fixed, unchanging steps are supported.
All navigation must follow one linear path.
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript conditions can change which steps or elements appear based on data or user input.
whyWrong: OmniStudio supports conditional logic.
Steps do not have to remain the same for every user.
An OmniScript can branch instead of following one fixed path.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an Integration Procedure return to the component that called it?
options: A command to delete the caller
A replacement for the caller’s input values, with no other output
Output data for the caller, such as an OmniScript or FlexCard
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Integration Procedure returns output data to its caller, such as an OmniScript or FlexCard.
whyWrong: An Integration Procedure does not exist to delete the calling component.
It can return results; it does not only replace input values.
Logging may be useful, but returning data is the purpose described.

sampleQuestions.question: Which method can teams use to deploy OmniStudio components?
options: Data Loader with a CSV file for every component type
FlexDeploy or a source-driven deployment process
sampleQuestions.explanation: Teams can deploy OmniStudio components with FlexDeploy or a source-driven deployment process.
whyWrong: Change Sets are not the only deployment method.
Workbench is not the only deployment method.
Data Loader moves records, not OmniStudio component definitions.

sampleQuestions.question: What does OmniScript Save behavior control?
options: When and how the OmniScript state is saved
Validation rules on Salesforce objects only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Save behavior controls when and how an OmniScript saves its state.
whyWrong: Save behavior is about persistence, not only navigation.
Save behavior changes how script state is stored.
Validation Rules check data; they do not control when the OmniScript saves its state.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio component can call Apex through a Remote Action?
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Integration Procedure can use a Remote Action to call an Apex class.
whyWrong: This component can call Apex through a Remote Action.
An OmniScript can invoke an Integration Procedure that calls Apex.
A FlexCard is primarily for compact data display and actions.

sampleQuestions.question: What do FlexCard merge fields do?
options: Replace a Data Mapper in the card's data source setup
Display changing values from the data source
sampleQuestions.explanation: Merge fields show values from a FlexCard’s data source in its display.
whyWrong: Merge fields do not replace Data Mappers.
Sending email is not their purpose.
Reports are created with reporting tools, not FlexCard merge fields.

sampleQuestions.question: Which practice supports reliable OmniStudio development?
options: Build each element for one use only.
Reuse components, handle errors, and test with users.
Avoid reusing components across solutions, even when they overlap.
Skip testing to speed up delivery.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusable elements, error handling, and user testing help make OmniStudio solutions easier to maintain and more reliable.
whyWrong: Single-use components can make solutions harder to maintain.
Reuse can reduce repeated work and support consistency.
Skipping tests can allow problems to reach users.
